articles.title: New Forest woman, 101, gets Ohio birthday card in mayoral mix-up
articles.summary: Care home mistakenly contacted  the mayor of Lyndhurst in Ohio instead of the Lyndhurst in Hampshire.
articles.body:
An unexpected card from a mayor in America was among hundreds of wishes sent to a care home resident for her 101st birthday.

Joan Hillman, resident of Hartwood House in the New Forest, said she felt "very lucky" to have received the cards, which were collected by the care home.

Among the cards was a transatlantic greeting from the mayor of Lyndhurst in Ohio after the care home accidentally contacted him instead of the mayor of Lyndhurst in Hampshire.

Charlotte Dean of the care home said the initiative "brought together generations, organisations and communities from both sides of the Atlantic, all united by the desire to make one remarkable lady feel loved and celebrated".

The idea to collect the cards came about when staff realised, having already received her milestone birthday card from the King at the age of 100, Hillman would not receive another royal card until her 105th birthday.

The care home said the response was "overwhelming", with schools, playgroups, Scouts and Girlguiding groups, carers' organisations, community centre groups, local businesses, care homes, and individuals sending birthday wishes.

The card from the mayor of Ohio, Patrick A.Ward, read: "It is my honor to extend our community's best wishes on your upcoming 101st Birthday!

"The changes that you have seen, technological, societal, economical, have been tremendous and perhaps, at times, a little scary to live through. Yet here you are.

Hillman, who grew up in London and has been at the care home for two years, said: "It means so much that so many people have thought about me on my birthday.

"I've never experienced anything like this and I feel very lucky."

Dean said: "For Joan, the experience was incredibly moving.

The care home said the cards showed the "extraordinary power of community spirit".

images.caption: Joan Hillman received hundreds of cards for her 101st birthday

articles.title: Richard III knife expert among engineers in Bradford exhibition
articles.summary: Sarah Hainsworth is among 50 engineers who have been photographed for the Bradford exhibition.
articles.body:
A professor who helped discover how Richard III died is among 50 people who have been photographed for an exhibition celebrating half a century of the Royal Academy of Engineering.

Prof Sarah Hainsworth, Pro-Vice-Chancellor at Durham University, will feature in the 50for50 exhibition at the National Science and Media Museum in Bradford.

She helped to establish the injuries that led to Richard's death, after his skeleton was discovered under a council car park in Leicester in 2012.

The exhibition was commissioned by the Royal Academy of Engineering and is travelling to venues across the UK as part of its 50th anniversary.

Hainsworth, who was born in Baildon and raised in Middleham, North Yorkshire, said the exhibition was a "fantastic opportunity to show to young people the diversity of engineering careers and what engineers do in reality".

She said: "I think when you look at it as an exhibition as a whole it just shows the breadth of the profession and the exciting things engineers work on."

She was included for her work as a materials and forensic engineer, studying what makes knives and other implements sharp and the forces involved in stabbing, as well as the tool marks left behind on bone.

"When the remains for Richard III were found under a car park in Leicester I got to look at the injuries to the skull, the ribs, the pelvis and to try and work with colleagues to determine what were the weapons that would have been used on the battlefield," she explained.

"That's the thing people really don't appreciate about engineering, they think we just do the same thing all the time but even if you've got a specialism the number of ways in which you can apply that specialism across engineering is really varied."

Taken by photojournalist Jude Vidal, from Harrogate, the photographs include some of the UK's most influential engineers.

Among them is Cath Noakes, Professor of Environmental Engineering for Buildings, at the University of Leeds.

Noakes said it was important to showcase the variety of work engineers do.

"My photo was actually taken during the pandemic because I did quite a lot of work on airborne transmission of infection and how we can manage that, which helped everybody with guidance during the pandemic," she said.

"People have this vision of an engineer as somebody who works with tools or works on a site somewhere, but it's so broad.

"You've got people working in biomedical, you've got people who are working more on computer models for how we predict the climate's going to affect flooding in cities."

Vidal said it had been inspiring to meet the engineers who were "genuinely good people trying to do good things all the time".

"Engineers are incredibly creative. You don't think of them as creative people, but you have to be creative to do the problem solving that they do," she said.

"There's a great mix of being incredibly creative and collaborative, but also the scientific edge you need to enable them to do the things they do."

articles.title: 1 dead, at least 12 injured after elderly driver plows into group of cyclists in North Carolina
articles.summary: One cyclist was killed and at least 12 others were injured after a driver, suspected to be impaired, plowed into a group of cyclists in North Carolina.
articles.body:
One cyclist was killed and at least 12 others were injured after a driver, suspected to be impaired, plowed into a group of cyclists in North Carolina.

Donald Robert Morris-Jones, 76, was driving on Optimist Farm Road in Wake County on Saturday morning when he crossed the center line and struck the group of cyclists, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said. The incident unfolded about 14 miles southwest of Raleigh.

After striking the group, the vehicle traveled away from the scene then ran off the left side of the roadway and crashed into a ditch a half a mile away from the cyclists, officials said.

The North Carolina State Highway Patrol responded to the scene just after 9:30 a.m.

One cyclist died as a result of the crash and at least a dozen more were hurt, authorities said. Their injuries range from minor to serious, and several were transported to hospitals for treatment.

Highway Patrol identified the deceased victim as Patrick Allen Turner, 63, of Cary, North Carolina.

Morris-Jones was arrested and charged with death by vehicle, seven counts of serious injury by vehicle, eight counts of hit and run, driving while impaired, reckless driving and drive left of center, according to Highway Patrol.

"Impairment is suspected to be a factor in the crash," the agency said.

Morris-Jones was being held in the Wake County Detention Center on $1 million bail.

images.caption: A car hit several people riding bicycles today near Raleigh, North Carolina, killing at least one person and injuring 20 others.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: Aposta de Goiânia ganha sozinha R$ 59,5 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogador acertou as seis dezenas e levou sozinho o prêmio máximo. Veja números sorteados.
articles.summary: O sorteio da Mega-Sena premiou um único bilhete registrado na Casa Lotérica Ponto Certo com R$ 59,5 milhões; confira as dezenas sorteadas neste domingo.
articles.body:
Uma aposta de Goiânia levou sozinha o prêmio máximo de R$ 59.526.903,72 da edição da Mega-Sena sorteada neste domingo (8). A aposta que acertou os números 22 - 25 - 29 - 37 - 46 - 54 foi registrada na Casa Lotérica Ponto Certo, localizada no Setor Leste Universitário, em Goiânia.

A aposta foi registrada como jogo simples (e não bolão). O ganhador resgistrou apenas os seis números sorteados.

Em Goiás, outras duas apostas marcaram cinco números e levaram R$ 23,2 mil cada. Os jogos que levaram a quina foram registrados em Anápolis (canais eletrônicos) e Pires do Rio (Semar Loterias).

O sorteio de número 3083 foi realizado neste domingo (8) no Espaço da Sorte, em São Paulo (SP).

O concurso premiou 61 apostas apostas com a quina, que levaram R$ 23.220,26 cada. Outras 3.117 apostas fizeram quatro acerto e levaram R$ 649,17 cada.

articles.title: Mãe se emociona ao desejar boa sorte para filha no Enem em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Para mãe, Alexandra da Rosa, é preciso 'amor e paciência' dos pais com filhos candidatos. Enem ocorre neste domingo (8) e em 15 de novembro.
articles.summary: Para mãe, Alexandra da Rosa, é preciso 'amor e paciência' dos pais com filhos candidatos.
articles.body:
Alexandra da Rosa abraça a filha antes da realização da prova do Enem em Florianópolis — Foto: Cristiano Gomes/NSC TV

A mãe Alexandra da Rosa ficou emocionada ao dar um forte abraço na filha, Cássia Vildner, antes da prova do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) em Florianópolis na tarde deste domingo (8). "A gente vê um esforço diário de uma filha, cinco anos de cursinho e ela não desistir", resumiu.

Antes do fechamento dos portões, Alexandra, que é professora, estava com a família na frente do Instituto Nacional de Educação (IEE), no Centro de Florianópolis. Ela acredita que o apoio é importante.

"Realmente é um sonho, ela acredita, é o futuro dela. E nós, como pai e mãe, a gente tem que estar do lado e arrumando o caminho para ela trilhar. E esperar que tudo dê certo", declarou.

"Tem que ter muito apoio, muita paciência, pouca cobrança. Porque não é fácil. E aquela famosa frase: 'Não pergunte como foi a prova, espera, porque tem mais uma ainda'. Deixa seguirem no tempo deles. É amor e paciência. É isso que pai e mãe têm que ter", resumiu.

O Enem ocorre neste domingo, com segundo dia de provas em 15 de novembro.

Alexandra da Rosa deseja boa sorte para a filha antes do Enem em Florianópolis — Foto: Cristiano Gomes/NSC TV

Quem fizer a prova poderá acompanhar no g1, a partir das 18h30 de domingo (8), a correção das questões, o gabarito extraoficial e vídeos sobre o primeiro dia do Enem.

articles.title: Asfalto cede e cratera 'engole' carro em Bauru | G1
articles.standfirst: Motorista teve ferimentos leves após abertura de buraco provocada por rompimento de galeria no Jardim Carolina, na madrugada deste domingo. Caso ocorreu quatro dias após caminhão cair em outra cratera que se abriu no Pousada da Esperança.
articles.summary: Cratera em Bauru abre no Jardim Carolina e engole carro de motorista de aplicativo, que foi resgatado com ferimentos leves após o rompimento de uma galeria pluvial.
articles.body:
O carro de um motorista de aplicativo foi "engolido" após o asfalto ceder e abrir uma cratera de aproximadamente três metros de largura e seis de comprimento na madrugada deste domingo (8), na quadra 4 da Rua Altair Leite de Campos, no Jardim Carolina, em Bauru (SP).

Segundo o relato do motorista, ele transitava pelo trecho quando a via cedeu repentinamente, fazendo o veículo tombar. Ele ficou preso dentro do automóvel.

Carro é 'engolido' por cratera após asfalto ceder durante a madrugada em Bauru — Foto: Bauru na Rua/Reprodução

Um motociclista que passava pelo local prestou os primeiros socorros e ajudou no resgate. A vítima deu entrada no Hospital de Base de Bauru (HBB), onde permaneceu em observação médica até as 7h30, quando foi liberada.

De acordo com apuração da TV TEM , o incidente foi provocado pelo rompimento de uma galeria de águas pluviais, que também danificou a rede de esgoto da via.

Carro é 'engolido' por cratera após asfalto ceder durante a madrugada em Bauru — Foto: Marcus Vinicius Anjos/TV TEM

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Bauru informou que o veículo envolvido na ocorrência de afundamento do asfalto, na quadra 4 da Rua Altair Leite de Campos, no Jardim Carolina, já foi retirado do local pela Companhia de Saneamento de Bauru (CSB). A companhia dará continuidade aos serviços de reparo da rede de esgoto e recomposição do solo.

A administração municipal acrescentou que a Secretaria de Infraestrutura acompanha a ocorrência desde a manhã deste domingo (8) e realizará, nesta segunda-feira (9), uma avaliação das condições da rede de galerias de águas pluviais para verificar a necessidade de intervenções complementares.

Quatro dias antes, na manhã de quarta-feira (4), um caminhão carregado com terra também foi parcialmente "engolido" pelo asfalto após o solo ceder e abrir uma cratera no bairro Pousada da Esperança 1, em Bauru.

O motorista não se feriu. Segundo ele, ao tentar desviar de um carro estacionado na via, o caminhão acabou caindo no buraco, enquanto o asfalto cedia ao redor do veículo. Uma equipe do Departamento de Água e Esgoto (DAE) foi acionada e esteve no local para realizar os reparos.

articles.title: Fã que cantou com Marília Mendonça viraliza em campo com o Palmeiras | G1
articles.standfirst: Valentina Falanga entrou de com zagueiro alviverde em goleada sobre o Corinthians; aos 13 anos, jovem que cantou com sertaneja em 2021 coleciona milhões de visualizações na web.
articles.summary: A pequena Valentina Falanga, de 13 anos, viralizou nas redes sociais esbanjando carisma e conhecendo diferentes artistas e celebridades.
articles.body:
Palmeirense desde que se conhece por gente, Valentina Falanga, de 13 anos, teve a oportunidade de entrar em campo com os jogadores do Palmeiras em uma partida do Campeonato Brasileiro. O momento viralizou nas redes sociais, assim como outros, onde a garota esbanja carisma ao lado dos jogadores e celebridades. Assista acima .

Valentina foi a última fã a subir no palco com a cantora Marília Mendonça , em Sorocaba (SP), no dia 1º de novembro em 2021, quando a sertaneja fez seu último show.

Segundo a mãe, Monica Esposito, a menina nasceu com síndrome de Down e perdeu parte de uma das pernas após contrair meningite na infância. Mesmo utilizando prótese, Valentina não deixa que essas condições limitem sua energia e o entusiasmo para explorar o mundo e conhecer pessoas.

Valentina viralizou com o Palmeiras quando entrou em campo com Alexander Barboza — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Valentina viralizou após entrar em campo com o atleta Alexander Barboza, jogador argentino e naturalizado paraguaio, que atua como zagueiro no Palmeiras. O vídeo já acumula mais de 2 milhões de acessos e conta com 190 mil curtidas .

Nos comentários da publicação, os internautas celebraram a participação da menina no início da partida, pois a pequena teria trazido sorte ao "verdão".

Vlentina viralizou ao entrar em campo com os jogadores do Palmeiras — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A partida foi em 11 de outubro, no Nubank Parque, quando o Palmeiras venceu o Corinthians por 4 a 1 no Campeonato Brasileiro Série A. Além de Barboza, a pequena pôde conhecer o atacante Flaco López, o capitão Gustavo Gómez, o lateral Joaquín Piquerez, entre outros atletas da equipe.

Valentina Falanga com jogadores do Palmeiras — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Carismática e curiosa, Valentina já subiu ao palco com MC Livinho, Léo Santana, Ana Castela, Zé Felipe e a dupla Maiara & Maraisa. Ela também conversou com Roberto Carlos, Jeninho, Luan Pereira e a dupla Henrique & Juliano.

Nas redes sociais, outro vídeo de destaque mostra Valentina dançando o hit "Peão Todo Tatuado" ao lado de Jeninho. A gravação ultrapassa 1 milhão de acessos e 60 mil curtidas.

Segundo Monica, até mesmo o cantor Roberto Carlos, conhecido pelo estilo reservado no atendimento a fãs e imprensa, abriu uma exceção para receber ela e a filha.

"O Roberto Carlos fez uma exceção, porque ele é bem sistemático e não costuma atender ninguém. Ele nos recebeu e foi super legal. A Valentina até brincou e disse para ele casar comigo", lembrou a mãe.

A garota também conheceu o youtuber Luccas Neto e sua parceira de projetos, Giovanna Alparone, a Gi.

Cantou em último show da Marília Mendonça

Valentina era apenas uma criança de nove anos e ficou conhecida como a última fã a subir no palco para cantar com Marília Mendonça . A menina veio de São Caetano do Sul (SP) com a família apenas para ver o show no interior.

"Eu quero muito ver ela lá no céu. Eu amo ela. Muito. (...) Eu preciso ver ela, sabe? Quero muito ver ela. Eu sinto muita falta dela. Marilinha, obrigada, obrigada, obrigada por tudo", disse.

Valentina Falanga foi a última fã a subir no palco com Marília Mendonça em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Monica Esposito/Arquivo pessoal

Na época, a família da menina se programou para dormir em Sorocaba com o outro filho, de 15 anos. Momentos antes do show, a equipe da cantora permitiu a entrada no camarim. Assista à entrevista com Valentina :

A mãe de Valentina, Monica Esposito, também contou ao g1 que o hábito de ouvir música sertaneja fez com que a filha se apaixonasse pelas canções da artista.

"Ela (Valentina) aprendeu a gostar e aprendeu a cantar as músicas, do jeitinho dela, mas ela sabe todas. Ela sabe até algumas mais do que eu. (...) A Marília era uma pessoa maravilhosa. É uma grande perda. A Valentina deu muito trabalho, para explicar pra Valentina e ela não queria entender (sobre a morte) e, ao mesmo tempo, ela é inteligente, ela entende. Mas até hoje ela chora pedindo pra Marília Mendonça descer do céu, ou que ela quer ir visitar a Marília lá em cima", disse.

Um ano depois do encontro com a cantora, a menina viralizou na internet com um vídeo feito pela sua mãe. Nas imagens, Valentina está na varanda de casa, olhando para o céu, cantando e chamando por Marília.

articles.title: Enem 2026 em Petrolina: Histórias de superação no primeiro dia | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato de 20 anos quer direito após pausa para cuidar da saúde mental; estudante de 17 anos faz o exame como 'treino' para biomedicina.
articles.summary: O Enem 2026 em Petrolina reuniu 15 mil inscritos, como João Paulo, que busca vaga em Direito após cuidar da saúde mental, e Lunara, que estreia como treineira.
articles.body:
ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - PETROLINA (PE) - João Paulo Batista Oliveira, de 20 anos, saiu cedo de casa, na zona rural, para pegar o transporte e fazer a prova no bairro Cidade Universitária, em Petrolina — Foto: Andressa Silva / g1 Petrolina

João Paulo Batista Oliveira, de 20 anos, vai enfrentar mais do que as questões de Ciências Humanas e Linguagens neste domingo (8), primeiro dia do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026. Em busca de uma vaga no curso de direito, ele superou a distância e problemas de transporte para chegar à Universidade de Pernambuco (UPE), em Petrolina , no Sertão do estado.

João Paulo prestou o exame pela primeira vez em 2024, para o curso de história. Dois anos depois, ele tenta uma vaga em direito com o objetivo de lutar, entre outras causas, contra a violência doméstica e o racismo. Morador do Projeto Maria Tereza, na Área 19, zona rural de Petrolina, ele precisou sair de casa às 9h para garantir a chegada com antecedência.

O intervalo de dois anos entre as provas foi necessário para cuidar da saúde mental. Ele contou que desenvolveu ansiedade e depressão durante o ensino médio, e precisou de um tempo para se recuperar e voltar a trabalhar.

“Fazer o Enem de novo este ano é uma maneira de dizer: 'eu estou voltando a sonhar'. Estou tentando de novo viver, porque a vida é longa, mas é curta”, refletiu João Paulo.

Além das questões emocionais, a logística foi um obstáculo. João Paulo relatou as dificuldades de transporte público para quem mora na zona rural de Petrolina. Segundo ele, a van que sai às 10h vai apenas até a Área 25, não cobrindo o trajeto até a Área 19, onde reside, o que exige uma caminhada de quase 1 quilômetro.

“Para a gente que mora na área rural e não tem transporte próprio, é muito difícil fazer uma faculdade. Então, este ano vou tentar direito e também um emprego na cidade [zona urbana] para poder me mudar para cá”, explicou.

ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - PETROLINA (PE) - Lunara Silva Capellaro, de 17 anos, estava acompanhada da mãe, para o primeiro dia do Exame no bairro Cidade Universitária, em Petrolina — Foto: Andressa Silva / g1 Petrolina

Já Lunara Silva Capellaro, de 17 anos, faz o Enem com foco no curso de biomedicina. Ainda no segundo ano do ensino médio, ela realiza a prova como treineira, acompanhada e apoiada pela mãe.

“É só um treino. Espero tirar uma nota média, mas que seja suficiente para me dar confiança para o próximo Enem”, disse Lunara.

Lunara estudou apenas na escola regular, sem o auxílio de cursinho pré-vestibular. Ela admitiu o nervosismo da estreia e contou que fez uma última revisão antes de sair de casa.

Em Petrolina, quase 15 mil estudantes se inscreveram para o Enem 2026. Neste domingo, os candidatos responderam a questões de Ciências Humanas, Linguagens e realizaram a redação.

Em todo o país, mais de 5 milhões de candidatos se inscreveram no exame deste ano , o maior número dos últimos anos, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep). Em 2025, foram 4,8 milhões de inscritos confirmados.

articles.title: Enem no Amapá: Aluna viaja 185km de barco para fazer a prova | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudantes de áreas ribeirinhas e de cinco municípios sem locais de prova recebem apoio de transporte e alimentação do Governo do Amapá para realizar o exame neste domingo (8).
articles.summary: Com apoio do governo, mais de 9 mil estudantes fazem o Enem no Amapá, incluindo jovens ribeirinhos que enfrentam horas de viagem para acessar os locais de prova.
articles.body:
Estudante do Bailique,Thayla Thauane Santos, de 18 anos. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Mais de 9 mil estudantes da rede pública do Amapá fazem as provas do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio ( Enem ) neste primeiro domingo (8). Em Macapá , a Escola Estadual Tiradentes funcionou como ponto de apoio, com almoço e transporte, para alunos vindos de 5 municípios onde não há aplicação do exame, sendo: Ferreira Gomes , Serra do Navio , Itaubal , Pracuúba e Cutias .

Para fazer a prova na capital, a estudante Thayla Thauane Santos, de 18 anos, precisou enfrentar horas de navegação no rio, cerca de 185 quilômetros. Ela é moradora da comunidade do Carneiro, no arquipélago do Bailique, distrito de Macapá , e cursa o ensino médio na Escola Estadual Igarapé do Carneiro.

"A viagem é exaustiva por causa da maresia e do horário, pois chegamos de madrugada. Mas vale a pena o esforço para quem quer alcançar algo na vida. Venho me preparando desde que entrei no ensino médio. Fiquei em 6º lugar na redação do programa Jovem Senador e é gratificante representar minha escola. Quero cursar enfermagem para ajudar a minha comunidade", contou Thayla.

Além de Thayla, outro morador da comunidade do Carneiro que precisou se deslocar até a capital foi Fabrício Braga dos Santos, de 20 anos.

"A viagem foi boa, apesar das dificuldades na preparação. Meu objetivo é tirar uma boa nota no Enem para conseguir entrar na faculdade", disse Fabrício.

Fabrício, morador do Bailique, enfrentou uma longa viagem fluvial para fazer o Enem. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Os dois estudantes do Bailique foram alocados em Macapá devido a um erro no sistema do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep), segundo a Secretaria de Estado da Educação (Seed).

Apesar da falha no cadastro do órgão federal, o Governo do Amapá assumiu os custos de transporte, acolhimento e alimentação dos alunos nos dois domingos de provas.

A secretária de Estado da Educação, Simone Guedes, explicou que a estrutura foi organizada para garantir suporte pedagógico, transporte e refeições aos candidatos antes e depois do exame.

"Montamos uma logística para atender 309 alunos. O Estado garantiu o transporte desde o município de origem, o acolhimento na chegada e a alimentação. Após a prova, eles retornam para a escola, jantam e seguem de volta para suas casas", destacou a secretária.

Simone Guedes, secretária de estado da educação. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

De acordo com a Seed, 9.049 alunos do 3º ano da rede pública estadual estão inscritos nesta edição. Como preparação, a pasta promoveu revisões pedagógicas ao longo do ano, incluindo o "Aulão Show Enem ", que reuniu cerca de 6 mil estudantes no Sambódromo de Macapá .

Estudantes dos municípios do interior do Amapá almoçaram na escola Tiradentes e seguiram para seus locais de prova. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Uma das novidades desta edição é a integração do Enem com o Sistema de Avaliação da Educação Básica (Saeb), determinada pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC). Com a mudança, a participação e o desempenho dos alunos na prova também serão computados para compor o índice educacional do estado.

Além disso, uma portaria publicada pelo MEC validou os dois domingos de aplicação do Enem como dias letivos na rede pública.

O Enem 2026 será realizado nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro. Principal mecanismo de acesso ao ensino superior no Brasil, a avaliação permite que os candidatos concorram a vagas em universidades públicas por meio do Sisu, além de bolsas de estudo do Prouni e financiamentos pelo Fies, conforme as regras de cada programa.

articles.title: Com chocolates e balas, aluna leva doces para 'ficar esperta' no Enem | G1

articles.summary: A estudante Amelly Nascimento, de 19 anos, é um dos 120,8 mil candidatos inscritos no estado que devem fazer o primeiro dia de prova neste domingo (08).
articles.body:
A estudante Amelly Nascimento, de 19 anos, realizou neste domingo (8) o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem), em Teresina . Ao g1, a jovem contou que levou cinco chocolates e mais balas de gelatina para se manter desperta durante a prova.

"Eu trouxe chocolates, olha só. Muito doce pra deixar a gente bem desperto, né? Fini, bis e o que eu ainda ganhei aqui. Só para eu não morrer. Para não ficar desligada. Ficar bem atenta ", brincou a jovem.

Amelly contou ainda que é o segundo ano em que tenta uma vaga no curso de Enfermagem.

"Estudei, estudei. Desde o começo do ano. Espero por Deus, que dê tudo certo. Todo esforço vale a pena" afirma Amelly

São mais de 72 mil candidatas, contra 48,7 mil candidatos, uma diferença superior a 23 mil inscrições. Ao todo, 120,8 mil pessoas estão confirmadas para fazer a prova neste domingo (8).

Os dados fazem parte do Painel Enem 2026, do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep). A ferramenta permite consultar indicadores por estado e município, incluindo faixa etária, situação escolar e atendimentos especializados.

No primeiro dia, os participantes responderão às questões de Linguagens, Códigos e suas Tecnologias, Redação e Ciências Humanas e suas Tecnologias. No segundo dia, serão aplicadas as provas de Ciências da Natureza e suas Tecnologias e Matemática e suas Tecnologias.

articles.title: Enem 2026: Mãe entrega RG para o filho minutos antes do portão fechar  | G1
articles.standfirst: Guilherme Lucena, de 17 anos, achava que tinha perdido o documento e registrou um boletim de ocorrência, mas não conseguiu entrar. Mãe dele achou o RG e conseguiu entregar minutos antes dos portões fechar em Rio Branco.
articles.summary: Guilherme Lucena, de 17 anos, achava que tinha perdido o documento e registrou um boletim de ocorrência, mas não conseguiu entrar. Mãe dele achou o RG e conseguiu entregar minutos.
articles.body:
ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - RIO BRANCO (AC) - mãe consegue entregar RG para o filho minutos antes do portão fechar — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

O estudante Guilherme Lucena, de 17 anos, quase fica sem fazer as provas do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026 neste domingo (8). É que ele achava que tinha perdido da Carteira de Identidade há alguns meses, registrou um boletim de ocorrência, mas não conseguiu entrar no local de provas, em Rio Branco.

Decepcionado, ele ligou para os pais buscá-lo na Unimeta e levá-lo para casa. A mãe dele começou a procurar o documento em casa, achou e conseguiu levar para o filho antes do portão fechar.

A mulher chegou ao local de prova do filho faltando cerca de 5 minutos para o portão fechar. Ela não quis falar sobre o assunto. A equipe do g1 registrou o momento em que a mãe entrega o documento para Guilherme na porta da faculdade.

ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - RIO BRANCO (AC) - Estudante achava que tinha perdido documento e foi barrado no local de prova — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

Ao entrar no carro para ir embora, a mãe de Guilherme falou que encontrou o documento nas coisas do filho.

"Acabei não encontrando minha identidade e, com isso, acabei sendo barrado. Fui atrás de um boletim de ocorrência para conseguir realizar a prova, tentei a identidade de forma digital", disse Guilherme.

No Acre, 26.550 pessoas estão inscritas para fazer o Enem neste ano . Os portões dos locais de prova abriram às 10h e fecharam às 11h, no horário local. A aplicação começa às 11h30.

Neste primeiro domingo, os participantes respondem a 90 questões objetivas, sendo 45 de Linguagens, Códigos e suas Tecnologias e 45 de Ciências Humanas e suas Tecnologias. Também precisam produzir uma redação.

O tempo de aplicação termina às 17h. Os candidatos podem levar o caderno de questões somente nos últimos 30 minutos da prova.

Para chegar aos locais de aplicação, os participantes contam com ônibus gratuitos em Rio Branco. A gratuidade é concedida mediante apresentação de documento de identificação e cartão de confirmação do Enem.

ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - RIO BRANCO (AC) - Guilherme Lucena achava que tinha perdido o documento e quase não consegue entrar — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

Para fazer a prova, é obrigatório apresentar documento oficial com foto e levar caneta esferográfica de tinta preta, fabricada em material transparente. O cartão de confirmação não é obrigatório, mas o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) recomenda que os candidatos levem o documento para consultar informações sobre o local de aplicação.

O segundo dia de provas será no próximo domingo (15), quando os participantes responderão a outras 90 questões, desta vez de Matemática e Ciências da Natureza.

ENEM 2026 - DOMINGO (8) - RIO BRANCO (AC) - mais de 26 mil candidatos fazem as provas no Acre — Foto: Jhenyfer de Souza/g1

O Enem é uma das principais formas de ingresso no ensino superior brasileiro. As notas podem ser utilizadas em processos seletivos de universidades públicas e privadas e em programas como o Sistema de Seleção Unificada (Sisu), o Programa Universidade para Todos (Prouni) e o Fundo de Financiamento Estudantil (Fies).

Além da seleção de estudantes para o ensino superior, a partir de 2026 o exame também passa a ser utilizado pelo governo federal como instrumento de avaliação da qualidade do ensino médio, nos moldes do Sistema de Avaliação da Educação Básica (Saeb).

articles.title: The West in pictures: Knitted poppies and Aardman cider TV advert
articles.summary: A round-up of the best photographs from around the region this week.
articles.body:
As thousands of people gather to pay their respects and mark Remembrance Sunday, knitters have been out in force decorating buildings and war memorials with poppies across the West.

Salisbury Cathedral has been attracting thousands of visitors for its latest light show, Sarum Lights: Great Journeys.

Elsewhere, antelopes have been introduced to Longleat and Aardman has collaborated with local cidermakers for a Christmas TV advert.

Here is a round-up of the best photographs from across the region this week.

Light show: Salisbury Cathedral has been lit up this week with its latest show from artist Luxmuralis. Thousands of people have been visiting the event, Sarum Lights: Great Journeys, which has featured famous voyages through moving projections and soundscapes.

New species: Staff at Longleat are celebrating the arrival of 12 female southern lechwes - a type of antelope native to the wetlands of south-central America. The animals have been introduced in the safari as part of the park's 60th anniversary festivities.

Charity mascot: More than 35 knitters from the Swindon Big Knit group have created a life-size Pudsey Bear from 300 hand-knitted yellow squares to help raise funds for Children in Need.

Festival of Light: Visitors to Longleat this winter can follow the glow of more than 1,000 spectacular lanterns. The display covers a 2.5km (1.5 mile) trail through the estate and conjures up legendary worlds of myth and magic.

Rock memorabilia: A guitar used by Johnny Marr after his split from The Smiths is going under the hammer in Wiltshire next month. The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster is expected to fetch up to £30,000.

Knitted cascade: This poignant postbox topper was spotted in Edington this week ahead of events across the county for Remembrance Sunday.

Still going strong: Colin Shearn, 80, said he had no plans to retire from his job operating a loading shovel at Green Ore on the Mendips, despite his age. He said "as long as I can climb in and out, I'm alright".

Bus tour: Reach youth centre in South Petherton launched its National Tour this week, alongside Yeovil MP Adam Dance, who used the service as a child and credits it with saving his life. The bus, loaded with food and messages of hope, will visit 50 youth centres around the country, from Dumfries and Skegness, to London and Plymouth.

Photographic talent: Josh Dury, from Somerset, received the Low Light Award of the British Photographic Awards 2026 at a recent ceremony in London. Dury is a landscape astrophotographer and captures images of the night sky along with Earth's natural landscapes.

Green makeover: Plants and flowers have been added to the Forest Green Rovers changing room to help relieve stress for the players. One of the team described it as "like the Amazon Rainforest in there".

Still standing: These flamingos are part of the flock at Slimbridge Wetland Centre. Sir Peter Scott brought the first Chilean variety to the UK in 1961 and some of the current birds are now over 60 years old.

Red sky at night: This stunning image was captured at Elmore by one of our BBC Weather Watchers.

Blooming marvellous: Congratulations from local MP Simon Opher were well deserved for Stonehouse in Bloom which won the Gold, Best Small Town award and is the overall winner at this year's Britain in Bloom Awards.

Prestigious honour: Josh Taylor, senior site manager at the new 250-home Ellenbrook development, in Moreton-in-Marsh, has won a major award. He was given the National House Building Council (NHBC) Seal of Excellence for the second consecutive year.

Golden evening: Another stunning sunset was captured in Gloucestershire this week as the camera caught these striking rays of light across the peaceful landscape.

Festive first: Thatchers Cider has unveiled its first-ever Christmas TV advert, created in partnership with Bristol's Aardman Animations. Set at Myrtle Farm in Winscombe, Somerset, it features animated versions of cidermaker, Martin Thatcher, and Myrtle the dog.

Inconsistent campaign: Bristol City's 2-1 defeat to Wolverhampton Wanderers this week was the Robins third in a row at home and leaves them 15th-placed in the Championship.

Immersive experience: A new holographic show was projected into the nave of St Mary Redcliffe church this week. The 30-minute spectacular told the story of the history of Bristol through light, sound and storytelling.

Lest we forget: Lympsham WI members have created this knitted poppy display for the village memorial for Remembrance Sunday.

Cycling tribute: Holley James from Keynsham cycled 58 miles (93km) from Bristol to Weston-super-Mare carrying a scarf and a packet of jelly babies in memory of her grandmother. She raised £715 for Bristol and Weston Hospitals Charity after seeing first-hand the care shown to both her father and grandmother by hospital staff.

articles.title: Grenfell survivors’ NHS support service faces funding cut
articles.summary: Councillors call for long-term funding for the service ahead of the fire’s 10th anniversary.
articles.body:
An NHS service supporting people affected by the Grenfell Tower fire faces a funding cut from next year, Kensington and Chelsea councillors have heard.

The Grenfell Health and Wellbeing Service offers therapies and groups to survivors, bereaved families and the wider community.

NHS England is reducing its funding and no service has been confirmed beyond 2029, a council meeting was told.

NHS West and North London Integrated Care Board (ICB), which funds the service, said no decisions had been made and existing support remained in place.

NHS England committed £50m to the community's recovery in 2018, which funded the service. The ICB has bid for £1.8m to continue it, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

The fire in June 2017 killed 72 people. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has said it will make charging decisions before the 10th anniversary on 14 June 2027.

Lucy Knight, the Kensington and Chelsea council's lead member for adult social care and public health, said "no-one should be left worrying" about whether their care would still be there.

She said the NHS accepted the period ahead could be especially hard for the community, and now was not the time to change the model of care to fit a smaller budget unless it could still meet people's needs.

A cross-party motion asked the council to tell the ICB and local NHS trust that survivors and the bereaved remained a top priority, and to urge NHS England to confirm long-term funding.

Representatives of the ICB and Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust (CNWL), which runs the service, will attend a council scrutiny meeting in December.

In a September update, the service said support would "not simply stop".

The ICB said its priority was making sure future arrangements met the needs of those affected. It said local people were helping to shape proposals, which it aimed to finalise as soon as possible.

NHS England said it supported efforts to ensure people affected could continue to get the care they needed.

articles.title: Floods in Gaza leave tens of thousands without shelter
articles.summary: Civil Defence reports over 1,500 emergency calls as thousands of tents and shelters destroyed after heavy rains.
articles.body:
Flooding caused by heavy rains has damaged shelters and tents belonging to tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians across the Gaza Strip, authorities said.

Reporting from Gaza City in northern Gaza on Sunday, Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim al-Khalili said the makeshift tents many Palestinians have been forced to live in do not provide adequate shelter from harsh weather.

“The latest storm exposed just how fragile the protection is. In just a few hours, heavy rains and strong winds tore through shelters families had spent days trying to reinforce,” al-Khalili said.

He reported seeing soaked mattresses, pillows and clothes, saying nearly 400,000 displaced Palestinians are sheltering in locations considered “highly vulnerable” to more flooding.

Ahmad Alhendawi, regional director for the Middle East, North Africa and Eastern Europe at Save the Children International, said the situation was “heartbreaking” and “entirely foreseeable”.

“Our staff in Gaza tell us that over the weekend, while families slept, water flooded their tents and engulfed entire camps. Children shivered in the bitter cold without winter clothing, and families lost the few belongings they had left,” he said in a statement.

“This is not simply the result of bad weather. Tents, shelter kits and fuel are waiting at Gaza’s borders while children sleep in floodwater, because the Israeli authorities are blocking their entry. This is a choice, and children are paying the price,” he added.

Heavy rain and strong winds have hit Gaza since late Friday, flooding 70,000 tents and bringing down dozens of walls, according to the Government Media Office.

The flooding comes amid a humanitarian crisis in Gaza, as Israel continues to impose severe restrictions on aid supplies to the war-ravaged territory.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Abu Amra said displaced families whose shelters were flooded had not received food aid since early Saturday.

Jonathan Veitch, UNICEF special representative in Palestine, said the majority of people are living in “terrible conditions” and called for more funding to provide much-needed aid.

Gaza’s Government Media Office reports the storm caused damage estimated at $3m. But relief organisations have been struggling for years to bring in relief and support.

The Gaza Civil Defence said it received at least 1,500 emergency calls. The agency said more than 2,000 buildings are at risk of collapse and that at least 300,000 tents are needed to provide adequate shelter for displaced people affected by the weather conditions.

Israel’s genocidal war, which began on October 7, 2023, has devastated homes and infrastructure in Gaza, and continuing restrictions on aid, shelter supplies and reconstruction materials have hampered relief efforts.

More than 74,640 people have been killed since the genocidal war began on October 7, 2023, in response to a Hamas-led attack on southern Israel. Since a “ceasefire” took effect in October 2025, Israel has killed at least 1,610 Palestinians.

articles.title: Vinted and eBay could be included in under-16 social media ban, minister says
articles.summary: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.
articles.body:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.

Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".

The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.

Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."

It came after the Sunday Times reported that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.

The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.

Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".

Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.

The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.

A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".

"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.

An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".

"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.

The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.

YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.

A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".

That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.

It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted.

But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep".

He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective."

The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year.

Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach.

In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced.

Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.

Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective.

"But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services."

articles.body: A group of current and former Microsoft employees is circulating an open letter accusing the company of chasing artificial intelligence at the cost of its own people, customers and climate goals. The letter has drawn fresh attention after Microsoft offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its workforce. It is the largest such offer in the company’s history.Signed “Concerned Microsoft Workers,” the letter says that for many staff, “working at Microsoft has become joyless and demoralizing.” It ties the slump in morale to the period when the company ramped up its AI investments. It also points to heavy workloads, constant reorganisations and the threat of being replaced by AI.According to a report by The New York Times, the letter began doing the rounds among colleagues before the October 26 buyout announcement. It asks Microsoft to involve employees in decisions about how AI is built and used, and to stop linking AI use to rewards or reprimands.Microsoft employees say mandatory AI tools are making their work worseThe letter is blunt about what AI adoption looks like on the ground. Workers say they are pushed to use AI tools in almost every part of their jobs, often with little or no training and no reason given beyond speed. The result, they write, is a costly cycle of learning new tools, cleaning up poor AI output and rolling back weak features.The complaints go beyond the office. The signatories claim the company’s own research shows AI agents do not put user safety first, and that internal planning documents describe ways to get people hooked on AI products. They also object to secretive data centre projects, contracts with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Israeli military, and what they call circular investments among a handful of AI firms.Their demands fall under three headings: no AI without worker input and protections, no AI without community protections, and no trading away environmental promises for AI. On the last point, they want Microsoft to recommit to being carbon negative, water positive and zero waste by 2030. The group is open to full-time staff, employees of subsidiaries like GitHub and LinkedIn, vendors, interns and contractors.Microsoft buyout covers employees in India, US, UK and CanadaThe Voluntary Exit Offer went to eligible employees at level 70 and below in participating teams across India, the US, the UK and Canada. Sales and some engineering teams were left out. Those who accept get at least eight weeks of base pay, with the amount rising by level and tenure. They have until December 9 to decide and would leave on December 31.In a note to staff, chief people officer Amy Coleman called it “a new choice to make that transition now with support.” The company expects fewer than 5% of eligible employees to sign up.This is Microsoft’s second buyout of 2026. In April, about 8,600 long-serving US employees were offered early retirement, and roughly 30% took it. In July, the company cut about 4,800 jobs, including a fifth of its Xbox workforce. That followed 10,000 layoffs in 2023 and more than 15,000 in 2025. Headcount stood at 223,000 in June, down 5,000 from a year earlier.Microsoft's record profits and AI spending sit beside raises below 1%The timing has not gone unnoticed inside the company. Two days after the buyouts were announced, Microsoft reported quarterly profit of $36.6 billion, up 32%, on revenue of $92.3 billion. Capital spending, mostly on data centres, rose 30% to $45.2 billion. The company expects to spend about $170 billion this calendar year.Employees told The New York Times that merit raises this year were unusually small, in some cases under 1%. At a town hall last month, a question on how leadership balanced over $100 billion a year in AI spending against flat rewards drew more than 80 reactions, about double what most questions got.Gretchen Thomas, a 57-year-old design leader who left in September after five years, told the publication her stock award was cut partly for not consistently showing speed and a willingness to experiment, including with AI. “I just can’t believe how grim it’s gotten just in the last three years,” she said.Coleman has said the buyouts are not linked to how AI is changing work, the report noted. She did not rule out future layoffs either.For those who stay, the bigger worry is the work left behind. Several employees said they do not expect departing colleagues to be replaced, which leaves more on their plates as the AI push carries on.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Cynicism and brutality': Russia targets Ukrainian rescue workers at site of Zaporizhzhia bombing that killed 55
articles.summary: A Russian FPV drone struck emergency workers carrying out search and rescue operations at the site of an earlier airstrike in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia
articles.body: A Russian FPV drone struck emergency workers carrying out search and rescue operations at the site of an earlier airstrike in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region on Sunday, damaging specialised rescue equipment. No personnel were injured, Ukraine's State Emergency Service (SES) said.The attack took place in the village of Komyshuvakha, where rescue operations have been underway for seven days following a Russian airstrike on November 2 that killed at least 55 people.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said more people could still be trapped under the rubble of the former school and shelter hit in the earlier attack."Absolute cynicism and brutality," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, accusing Russian forces of deliberately targeting the site while emergency crews were working there.The November 2 attack struck a former school being used as a humanitarian aid distribution centre and shelter for residents of Komyshuvakha and neighbouring villages. The facility was hit by multiple Russian guided bombs as people gathered to receive humanitarian assistance.The death toll had risen to 55 by November 7, while around 50 people remained missing, according to Ukraine's military intelligence agency. Many of the bodies recovered have yet to be identified, with DNA analysis underway.Among those killed were six emergency and police personnel, including two State Emergency Service workers and four police officers. Three of the police officers were killed near the former school.At a farewell ceremony in Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, colleagues and relatives paid tribute to six police officers killed in the attack. Three residents who also died were laid to rest in the city.The attack on Sunday adds evidence to repeated Ukrainian accusations that Russian forces carry out successive strikes on the same location to hit emergency responders arriving after an initial attack, a tactic commonly described as a "double-tap" strike.You use AI every day. articles.title: Will Eisenkot be able to form Israel’s next gov’t amid divided opposition?
articles.summary: Former army chief has 28 days to cobble together a ruling coalition after President chose him over incumbent Netanyahu.
articles.body:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been given the opportunity to form a new government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections, raising the possibility of an end to his long tenure in power.

President Isaac Herzog selected the former military chief on Saturday, following consultations with political parties. Eisenkot has 28 days to cobble together a coalition to form a government. If he fails to form a new administration within that period, he can seek a 14-day extension.

“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, posted on X.

However, the 66-year-old faces a difficult challenge as many of the opposition parties hold sharply conflicting positions on national security, religion and the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory.

Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has a 61-seat majority in Israel’s 120-member parliament, the Knesset.

As a result, Arab-led parties hold a potentially decisive role in determining who governs Israel, even as Eisenkot and his prospective partners refuse to rely on their support.

So what do we now know about Eisenkot’s possible paths to power, and can he succeed in unseating Netanyahu?

Can Eisenkot unite Israel’s divided opposition?

Eisenkot’s potential coalition spans his Yashar party, the centre-left Democrats led by Yair Golan, Naftali Bennett’s centre-right Together party and Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu (Israel Our Home).

Overall, they control 48 seats, well short of a majority.

Arab-led parties Ra’am (United List) and the Joint List (comprising three parties – Hadash, Ta’al and Balad) – jointly holding 19 seats – have endorsed Eisenkot’s attempt to form a government. Their backing would give the broader anti-Netanyahu camp a combined 67 seats.

Hadash is an Arab-Jewish party, Ta’al advocates for the rights of Palestinian citizens of Israel, and Balad demands equal rights for all its citizens.

However, Eisenkot has ruled out bringing Arab parties into his government, while Lieberman has repeatedly rejected forming a minority administration dependent on their support. Golan’s Democrats have been more willing to partner with Ra’am and the Joint List.

“We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” Golan said after the election.

How many seats does Netanyahu’s coalition have now?

Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist coalition has fallen from the 64 seats it secured in 2022 to 53, eight seats short of a majority.

His Likud is the largest individual party with 27 seats, while Eisenkot’s Yashar won 21.

Netanyahu’s efforts to remain in power suffered a further setback when United Torah Judaism, a longtime ultra-Orthodox ally, declined to endorse him or any other candidate during consultations with Herzog.

While the decision hurts Netanyahu’s prospects of regaining power, it did not rule out the party supporting him in future coalition negotiations if their demands were met, particularly compulsory military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews, which they reject.

If Eisenkot is unable to put together a coalition, he could potentially lead a minority government backed by Arab parties from outside.

A minority government is formed when the parties holding cabinet positions do not collectively control a majority of seats in parliament. Instead, they depend on support from lawmakers outside the governing coalition to remain in power and pass legislation.

Eisenkot could establish such an administration with his four-party bloc relying on external parliamentary support from Ra’am and the Joint List .

Under this arrangement, the Arab-led parties would not necessarily receive cabinet positions or formally join the coalition.

They could instead negotiate policy concessions in exchange for their parliamentary support.

In 2021, Ra’am joined a government led by Bennett, becoming the first independent Arab party to participate in an Israeli governing coalition.

That administration collapsed after 18 months, mainly due to disagreements over the illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and Palestinian statehood. Most Israeli parties do not support the creation of a sovereign Palestinian state as part of the so-called two-state solution.

Netanyahu, who has been in power for most of the past 20 years, has openly rejected Palestinian statehood and has pushed settlement expansions that are the biggest hurdles in the realisation of Palestinian statehood. Settlements are considered illegal under international law.

What are the other possible paths to forming a government?

Beyond a minority government, Eisenkot could attempt to secure a parliamentary majority by bringing Israel’s two ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, into his coalition.

Together, they hold 13 seats, which would give Eisenkot’s bloc exactly the 61 seats required for a majority.

However, such an alliance would require compromises over military conscription exemptions for ultra-Orthodox religious students, an issue that has long divided Israeli politics.

Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have criticised the exemptions. But Lieberman has recently indicated that he is open to compromise.

While United Torah Judaism has refused to endorse Netanyahu, Shas backed the beleaguered prime minister.

Another option would be a unity government involving Eisenkot’s Yashar, Bennett’s Together party, Lieberman’s Israel Our Home and Netanyahu’s Likud.

Such an alliance would command 67 seats, but would require Eisenkot and his partners to abandon their central election pledge to remove Netanyahu from power.

If Eisenkot fails to form a government within the required time, Herzog could give Netanyahu an opportunity to form a governing coalition.

Should both leaders fail, parliament could nominate another candidate. If no government emerges after a process lasting 100 days, Israelis could be heading to the polls again.

The negotiations could determine not only who becomes Israel’s next prime minister, but also which political parties control key ministries and shape policies on the economy, military conscription and the occupied Palestinian territory.

Several members of Eisenkot’s opposition bloc have previously held senior government positions, including in the coalition that removed Netanyahu from power in 2021.

Bennett, who served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022, has long opposed the establishment of a Palestinian state and advocated annexing large parts of the occupied West Bank.

During Israel’s 11-day war on Gaza in May 2021, Bennett, then an opposition politician, backed Netanyahu’s military offensive in the Palestinian enclave. More than 250 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks.

Meanwhile, Lieberman served as finance minister in Bennett’s government and previously held the defence portfolio under Netanyahu.

He previously proposed swapping some Arab communities in Israel proper for Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank in the context of a final peace deal with the Palestinians.

Lieberman’s party backs illegal settlement expansion, including E1, and annexing all of Area C, 60 percent of the occupied West Bank already under full Israeli control. E1, which stands for East 1 settlement, is a 12sq km corridor with thousands of housing units. It will cut the West Bank into two parts.

Eisenkot himself served in Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet before leaving the government after disagreements over the conduct of the genocide in Gaza. He has not opposed the genocide but criticised Netanyahu for prioritising his political survival over security considerations.

He has called the idea of a Palestinian state “delusional”, and he supports “strengthening” illegal settlements.

Academic Neve Gordon says an Eisenkot government could bring notable changes to Israel’s domestic politics, particularly by reversing parts of Netanyahu’s judicial overhaul.

“If Eisenkot is able to establish a government, he will likely be able to stop the judicial overhaul by cancelling the legislation that the Netanyahu government put in place, particularly in relation to the way Supreme Court judges are chosen,” said the law professor at Queen Mary University of London.

Gordon also expects a new government to establish an independent inquiry into the October 7 attacks and potentially introduce legislation preventing politicians facing trial for serious offences from becoming prime minister.

Palestinian citizens of Israel, Gordon said, could also benefit if Arab-led parties support the government from outside the coalition.

“The government is likely to allocate funds to Palestinian towns, adding funds to neglected infrastructures, schools and the like, while also spending more money on policing in order to clamp down on crimes and the high murder rates,” he said.

When it comes to Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, Gordon expects far less change.

“Here the changes will be merely cosmetic,” he said, arguing that Eisenkot’s prospective coalition remains predominantly right-wing and opposed to Palestinian statehood.

Gordon suggested that a new government might attempt to restrain some Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, but questioned whether such efforts would succeed because of the close relationship between settlers and Israeli security forces.

“And I do not foresee any substantial change in policy in the Gaza Strip,” he said.

articles.title: 'Time is up': Nandy warns media industry to take abuse seriously in wake of Brand case
articles.summary: Lisa Nandy tells the BBC "many people" in the media industry have come forward to her.
articles.body:
Abuse in the media industry is probably still happening as organisations are not doing enough to protect women, the culture secretary has warned in the wake of Russell Brand's conviction.

Lisa Nandy told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "Time is up, it really is time for the media industry to take this seriously."

She added that since entering government, "many people" from within the industry had reached out to her "to allege that things have happened to them".

Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault after a four-week trial, following allegations from multiple women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.

Nandy was asked whether she believed there was still exploitation and abuse within the media industry, following the Brand trial and cancellation of Channel 4 reality show Married at First Sight after the BBC revealed rape allegations.

She said: "I do not see that much has changed in terms of the way that institutions in the media industry and across public life, including politics, deal with women who very bravely come forward to allege abuse."

Nandy added that there was often no protection and a "very heavy cost" for women who speak up in industries such as media and politics, pointing to power imbalances and short-term contracts some staff members are given.

"Hand on heart, I can't say to you as the culture secretary that this is not happening today. In fact, if I had to wager, I would say it is," she said.

Nandy said many had come forward from within the industry, including from the BBC.

But she added that the BBC had been an "exemplar" in signing up to the industry body to protect whistleblowers - the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority - and urged other organisations to follow suit.

A BBC spokesperson said the broadcaster "has made a significant commitment to improve its culture, processes and standards".

"Last year, following an independent culture review, we set out the behavioural expectations for everyone who works with or for the BBC and we were clear action would be taken if these were not met," the spokesperson added.

Starting his career as a stand-up comedian, Brand became a household name as a host of TV shows such as Big Brother's Big Mouth. He also had his own radio programmes on BBC Radio 2 and 6 Music.

During Brand's trial, he faced allegations from six women and was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault . The women revealed how Brand used his fame to force them into sexual activity.

Following his conviction, a BBC spokesperson said there could be "no place for the abuse of power", adding: "Across the industry we must work together to ensure that anyone who suffers at someone else's hand feels able to report it, that their concerns are taken seriously and that they are listened to."

The corporation restated its apology to staff who felt they could not speak up with concerns about Brand's behaviour when he worked at the BBC between 2006 and 2008, because he was seen as "too influential".

Channel 4, which aired Big Brother and its spin-off programmes at the time Brand was a presenter, said it recognised the "profound impact of these crimes".

articles.title: Killer’s chewing gum blows open 40-year-old murders, detective warns there may be more victims
articles.summary: Mitchell Gaff admitted to six rapes during state evaluations, yet a court later freed him. DNA evidence now ties him to two 1984 Everett murders.
articles.body: Decades before DNA evidence linked Mitchell Gaff to two Washington cold-case murders, he admitted to six rapes during state psychological evaluations, court records show. Years later, a judge ended his civil commitment, allowing him to live in the community without the restrictions imposed under Washington’s sexually violent predator program. Gaff pleaded guilty in April 2026 to the murders of Judith "Judy" Weaver and Susan Vesey. A Snohomish County Superior Court judge sentenced him to 50 years to life in prison in May. DNA FROM CHEWING GUM NAILS LONGTIME SEXUAL PREDATOR DECADES AFTER REIGN OF TERROR: REPORT His convictions have raised questions about other victims, given Gaff’s history of sexual violence before a court unconditionally released him from civil commitment in September 2018. Gaff later lived in Olympia under the alias "Sam Wise Price." CALIFORNIA SHERIFF FIGHTS PLAN TO HOUSE CONVICTED SEX PREDATOR NEAR GIRL SCOUT CAMP Dr. Katherine Ramsland, a forensic psychologist and author not affiliated with the case, told Fox News Digital that ignoring a predator's admissions carries dangerous risks. "Psychologically, if he'd confessed but discovered there'd be no consequence, he'd likely feel emboldened to potentially repeat it," Ramsland said. CONVICTED SERIAL RAPIST ORIGINALLY SENTENCED TO 124 YEARS WALKS FREE AFTER 20, SPARKING OUTRAGE Victims found strangled, sexually assaulted In June 1984, authorities found Weaver bound, sexually assaulted and strangled inside her apartment off Rucker Avenue in Everett. Investigators determined that Gaff had also sliced her clothing with a knife and set a fire in an attempt to destroy evidence. The investigation initially focused on Bill Richards, Weaver’s fiancé. Weaver’s daughters told investigators that the couple had a volatile relationship, according to KING 5 News. COLD CASE BREAKTHROUGH SOLVES TEEN KILLING AFTER SUSPECT LIVED FREE FOR DECADES: 'BETTER BE AFRAID' Richards remained a suspect until his death in 1994. In November 2023, Everett Police Department Detective Susan Logothetti submitted evidence from Weaver’s case for modern DNA testing, after obtaining a DNA sample through a ruse involving chewing gum. DISCARDED TRASH UNCAPS 41-YEAR-OLD MURDER CASE IN RITZY SEASIDE RESORT TOWN, AUTHORITIES SAY Authorities arrested Gaff in May 2024 after obtaining a DNA sample through the gum. DNA evidence then linked Gaff to Vesey’s murder. Authorities found her beaten and bound inside her Everett home on June 2, 1984, the morning of her 21st birthday. FORENSIC GENEALOGY UNMASKS COLD CASE SUSPECT AS STRANGLER, SEXUAL PREDATOR DECADES LATER: OFFICIALS Everett police said Gaff’s statements about the murders matched evidence investigators had gathered. Court records document a history of sexual violence In 1979, a jury convicted Gaff of first-degree burglary and second-degree assault after he bound a woman’s hands, repeatedly struck her with a pistol and smashed her head against concrete before she escaped, according to a Washington Court of Appeals opinion. Gaff received probation and work release. While still on probation in 1984, he broke into an Everett home and raped two teen sisters, ages 14 and 16, at knifepoint. A judge imposed an exceptional prison sentence of 138 months and revoked his probation, requiring him to serve his sentences consecutively. Before Gaff’s scheduled release from prison, Washington authorities petitioned to commit him to a secure facility as a sexually violent predator. CONVICTED PREDATORS FACE LIFETIME BARRIER UNDER GOP LAWMAKER’S SWEEPING VICTIM PROTECTION BILL During psychological evaluations, Gaff admitted to making obscene calls and committing sexual assaults, including six rapes. A jury found that he met the legal criteria for civil commitment, and the Washington Court of Appeals upheld the decision in April 1998. A psychologist who testified for the state diagnosed Gaff with sexual sadism and concluded that he posed a risk of reoffending. A defense expert, meanwhile, believed Gaff could live safely in the community under controlled conditions. Gaff moved to a halfway house before his 2018 release By 2005, state evaluators decided Gaff no longer required maximum confinement and approved his transfer to a less restrictive setting. In 2006, he left Washington’s Special Commitment Center on McNeil Island for a secure halfway house in Seattle’s SoDo district. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The agreement required GPS monitoring and supervision whenever Gaff left the facility. It also required him to give up his right to challenge his sexually violent predator status for eight years. Gaff remained under the state’s civil commitment system until September 2018, when a court dismissed his sexually violent predator petition and unconditionally released him from civil commitment, according to a 2019 report in The Olympian. "It's tricky to hold them beyond their sentence, and sometimes it means having to prove they're an imminent danger, not just a possible one," Ramsland said. articles.title: Cornwall artist who put camel in eye of needle plans exhibition
articles.summary: Artist makes tiny art that can fit in a needle's eye or on a cat's whisker.
articles.body:
Artist Adrian Thompson has created micro art from small pieces of gold that fit through the eye of a needle.

He said he enjoyed challenging himself to see what he could create.

Thompson, who works in Par, said: "As an artist sometimes it's you versus yourself. You want to see what you can create."

Each tiny piece takes up to a year to make and he is planning to display it at Bodmin's Discovering 42 science museum in December.

He started out transforming his gold dental filling, which had fallen out, into an angel when he lived in his home town of Solihull, near Birmingham.

Thompson used a file and said: "It slowly came to life over a period of about nine months, to my amazement."

He added: "Each times I picked it up I did a little bit more and a little bit more and got more inspiration. When I finally finished it I thought I really enjoyed it, I wonder what else I could be doing."

Thompson uses a microscope and had to customise watch maker's tools or make his own tiny tools to create his art.

He has placed his work in the eye of a needle, on the end of a needle and on a cat's whisker.

He also mounted a mini helicopter on an eyelash, which is one of the piece's people will be able to see in Bodmin.

Thompson created a microscope viewing dome for his pieces, which include a Ferrari horse on the end of a match stick valued at £100,000, the Aston Villa lion logo that was displayed at the club and a waving cat.

In the run-up to Halloween he made a microscopic gold witch flying out of an syringe point of a needle, along with a small Cornish pixie.

He said: "I've got many pieces to entertain people covering a range of different subjects.

"I've got quite a big car collection and what I call a 007 collection, which consists of Aston Martin wing DBS badge, and the 007 logo, all through the eye of a needle."

He added: "I've also created a standing Buddha out of white gold, a Chinese god called Caishen which fits on a meteorite, and a camel through the eye of a needle, so there is plenty of variety in my work."

articles.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
articles.summary: With 99 percent of votes counted, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s party wins 31 percent nationally.
articles.body:
South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) party faces a major setback after last week’s municipal elections, leaving it in a weak position in coalition talks to form city governments.

With 99 percent of the votes counted on Sunday, President Cyril Ramaphosa’s ANC had 31 percent nationally against 25 percent for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA).

That represents a drop of roughly 14 percentage points from its 2021 local elections performance.

Former President Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto weSizwe party won about 10 percent of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest of the ballots were split between hundreds of smaller parties.

Final results are expected to be announced at 6pm (16:00 GMT) on Sunday.

While still the largest party in South Africa, the ANC’s support has steadily eroded as voters grow increasingly frustrated with corruption and the party’s failure to tackle unemployment, which tops 34 percent more than three decades after the end of apartheid.

Failures in basic services, such as water and electricity, have also contributed to the ANC’s vote share falling in local elections over the past 15 years.

The party failed to win an outright majority in any of the eight major metro areas, including Johannesburg and Pretoria.

Since no party won more than 50 percent of the votes in many cities, including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up or hash it out with smaller parties to form municipal governments.

Parties will have 14 days to negotiate before city councils are formed.

ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the result “catastrophic” for the ANC but said the party would not go begging for positions when coalition talks begin soon.

“When the people tell us we have fallen short, … the honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order,” Mbalula said on Saturday.

In Johannesburg, the DA led the count with about 35 percent of the votes, compared with 20 percent for the ANC.

That could give DA veteran Helen Zille, who campaigned on fixing potholes and leaking water pipes, a good chance of becoming mayor, depending on the coalition agreements reached.

The DA said in a statement that it would initiate coalition discussions with “political parties that share a commitment to clean and accountable government, rooting out corruption, service delivery for all, the rule of law, and non-racialism”.

articles.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity
articles.summary: About 850,000 people lose power after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv.
articles.body:
More than 600,000 people in Ukraine’s eastern Dnipropetrovsk region are without electricity after a Russian overnight attack on an energy facility, a Ukrainian energy provider has said.

Residents across the Pavlohrad, Samarivskyi, Kamianske and Dnipro districts, as well as the city of Dnipro, faced electricity outages on Sunday, power company DTEK wrote in a Telegram post.

Engineers were at the scene attempting to restore the damaged facility, but “repairs are being complicated by repeated attacks”, DTEK said.

Ukraine is bracing for yet another harsh winter of war as Russia ramps up daily aerial attacks, raining down drones and missiles on the power network.

Another 250,000 Ukrainians were left without power in the Kharkiv region in northeastern Ukraine on Sunday after Russia struck an infrastructure facility there.

“No casualties have been reported, ” said Mykola Baksheyev, mayor of Zlatopil city, on Telegram.

“Power engineers are currently working to repair the damage; however, the exact timeframe for restoring the electricity supply remains unknown.”

The attacks came a day after Ukraine’s Ministry of Energy said a massive attack on energy facilities had plunged residents in five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused Russia of intensifying attacks to put pressure on Kyiv at United States-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Russia’s Ministry of Defence stated on its Telegram channel that its forces will “continue to carry out strikes against Ukrainian fuel and energy infrastructure facilities” that they say are used to aid the Ukrainian military.
